title: Await Copilot session teardown before config refresh
body:
Fixes #327125

A structural active-client configuration change refreshes the default Copilot chat by disposing and resuming its SDK session. Disposal previously started `session.disconnect()` without awaiting it, allowing the stale `session.destroy` request to terminate the newly resumed session with the same ID. The next turn then failed with `Holder terminated during creation`.

This change awaits the existing session teardown before clearing and resuming the default chat. Peer chats remain intact. A deterministic regression test holds disconnect open and verifies that dispose, resume, and send occur only after teardown completes.

- `npm run valid-layers-check`

body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in Agent Host using Copilot CLI 1.0.72
- VS Code Version: 1.131.0-insider (9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window, Agent Host Copilot session refresh
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Reproduced in Agent Host, AHP, persisted session events, and Copilot runtime logs. Sanitized causal timeline is included below.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Resume an existing `copilotcli` session in the Agents window.
2. Let the active client tool/plugin/MCP snapshot change structurally after the session was resumed, then send a message. This makes `ActiveClient.requiresRestart(...)` refresh the default chat.

The user-level repro is timing-dependent. A deterministic code-level repro is:

1. Hold the current SDK session's `disconnect()` promise open.
2. Register a structurally new client tool and send a message, forcing the config-refresh branch.
3. With the old code, observe that `_resumeSession()` starts before the held disconnect finishes.
4. Complete the old disconnect. Its `session.destroy` terminates the runtime session that was just resumed under the same session ID.
5. The turn fails with `Error: (query) Execution failed: Error: Holder terminated during creation`.

### Actual behavior

The turn fails before the first model response while the runtime builds settings and tools. Retrying in the same cached session fails again because the resumed session's shell-context holder is already terminal.

### Expected behavior

Refreshing a session after client configuration changes should fully tear down the previous runtime session before resuming the same session ID. The next message should run normally.

### Root cause analysis

The config-refresh branch in `CopilotAgent._sendMessage` called `clearDefaultChat()`. Disposing that chat disposes `CopilotSessionWrapper`, whose cleanup starts `session.disconnect()` without awaiting it. The code then immediately called `_resumeSession()` with the same SDK session ID.

The SDK's `disconnect()` sends `session.destroy` by session ID. Because teardown and resume were concurrent, the runtime completed `session.resume` first and processed the stale `session.destroy` afterward. Runtime session disposal calls shell shutdown, permanently terminating the shared `ShellContextHolder`. The resumed session object remained cached, but its next `buildSettingsAndTools` call could no longer create a shell context.

Observed UTC ordering:

- `13:00:11.523` — Agent Host detects `requiresRestart=true`, clears the cached default chat, and starts resume.
- `13:00:12.113` — Copilot runtime logs `Resumed session` for the same ID.
- `13:00:12.300` — Copilot runtime then logs `Closing session` for that ID.
- `13:00:12.348` — persisted events record `session.shutdown`.
- `13:00:12.350` — Copilot runtime logs `Destroyed session`.
- `13:00:19.238` — AHP emits `chat/error`: `Holder terminated during creation` from `getOrCreate` during `buildSettingsAndTools`.

The adjacent Notion authentication prompt and unrelated MCP startup failures are not causal.

### Proposed fix

Await `entry.destroySession()` before clearing the default chat and resuming the same SDK session ID. This keeps the old entry present until teardown completes, then disposes it and resumes. The wrapper's subsequent cleanup call to `disconnect()` is a no-op because the SDK session is already marked disconnected. Peer chats remain untouched.

title: git: remove repo from SCM when workspace folder is removed
body:
## Summary

Fixes #108757

When a workspace folder is removed from a multi-root workspace, the corresponding git repository was not being removed from the Source Control (SCM) panel.

## Root Cause

The original code in `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` used `getOpenRepository(folder.uri)` to find repositories to dispose. `getOpenRepository(uri)` internally checks `isDescendant(repoRoot, resourcePath)` which returns `false` when the repository root **is** the workspace folder itself (the most common case), because a path is not considered a descendant of itself. As a result, no repository was ever found and nothing was disposed.

## Fix

**1. Correct repository lookup on folder removal**

Instead of relying on the indirect URI lookup, the fix iterates `this.openRepositories` directly and checks whether each repository root is equal to or a descendant of any removed workspace folder.

**2. Prune stale `closedRepositories` entries**

When a repo was manually closed by the user (via "Close Repository") before the workspace folder was removed, its root path remained in the `closedRepositories` workspace state. This caused the repo to reappear in the SCM panel the next time the workspace was opened (step 4 of the original bug report). The fix now prunes these stale entries when their associated workspace folder is removed.

## Testing

Steps to reproduce (from issue #108757):
1. Create a multi-root workspace with two folders, each containing a git repo
2. Verify both repos appear in the SCM panel
3. Remove one folder from the workspace (right-click -> Remove Folder from Workspace)
4. The corresponding repo now immediately disappears from the SCM panel
5. Reopen the workspace
6. The removed repo no longer reappears

title: Fix race condition in modal editor part singleton creation
body:
## Summary

Fixes a race condition in modal editor part singleton creation identified while reviewing #326885.

EditorParts.createModalEditorPart awaited the ModalEditorPart creation (wait this.instantiationService.createInstance(ModalEditorPart, this).create(...)) *before* assigning 	his.modalEditorPart. If createModalEditorPart was called concurrently (e.g. two callers racing to open a modal editor), both calls could pass the "reuse existing instance" check and each create its own ModalEditorPart, resulting in duplicate modal editor parts/groups and duplicate onDidAddGroup events.

## Fix

- Track the in-flight creation as a promise (modalEditorPartCreatePromise).
- If a creation is already in flight when createModalEditorPart is called again, await that promise and apply the caller's options to the resulting singleton instance instead of starting a second creation.
- Preserves existing option-update behavior for both the "already created" and "creation in flight" cases.

This does **not** include the separate stable-ID change from #326885 — that should land separately.

## Testing

- createModalEditorPart is race-proof: concurrent creation returns same singleton instance (new test in modalEditorGroup.test.ts) fires 3 concurrent createModalEditorPart() calls via Promise.all and asserts:
  - all three calls resolve to the exact same instance/group
  - only one onDidAddGroup event fires
- Ran the full Modal Editor Group suite (42 tests) - all passing.
- 
pm run typecheck-client - 0 errors.

title: git - open nested repository when a file from it is opened later (fixes #327119)
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #327119

### Problem

Whether a nested git repository (one whose root sits below an already-open workspace/parent repository) gets registered depends on startup timing. If one of its files is visible when the window loads, the repository appears in Source Control; if the same file is opened later, it never does.

The cause is in `Model.onDidChangeVisibleTextEditors()`: it short-circuits when `getRepository()` returns a match for the editor resource. `getRepository()` matches purely by path ancestry over *already-open* repositories, so once an ancestor repository is open it always shadows a nested repository that has not been opened yet. During `doInitialScan()` the handler runs concurrently with the workspace folder scan, so the ancestor is usually not registered yet and the nested repository gets opened via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. After startup the ancestor always wins and `openRepository()` is never called.

### Fix

When the editor resource matches an already-open repository, probe for a `.git` folder/file between the resource and the matched repository root (one `fs.stat` per directory level, bounded by the repository root). If one is found, open that path with the existing `openRepository()`, which keeps all current behavior intact (repositories closed by the user, `git.ignoredRepositories`, unsafe repositories, parent repository handling, workspace trust). If nothing is found, the previous short-circuit behavior is unchanged.

### To test

1. Open a folder whose root is a git repository (the "parent").
2. Create a second git repository nested in a subfolder, e.g. `sub/nested` (`git init` plus a commit).
3. Start with no file from the nested repository visible, then open `sub/nested/<file>` from the Explorer.
4. Before this change: the nested repository never appears in Source Control; the git trace log shows `[Model][onDidChangeVisibleTextEditors] Repository for editor resource … already exists: <parent>`. With this change: the nested repository is registered as its own source control provider as soon as the file becomes visible.
5. Unchanged behavior to verify: files of the parent repository with no `.git` in between still short-circuit, repositories closed by the user stay closed, and detection still respects `git.autoRepositoryDetection` (`true`/`"openEditors"`).

labels.name: bug

body:

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (the cause is in the built-in Git extension, see analysis below)

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: <!-- fill in from Help > About --> (behavior verified in the Git extension source on `main`, 1.131.0, commit `396ff629`)
- OS Version: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open a workspace whose root folder is a git repository (the "parent").
2. Have a second git repository nested in a subfolder beneath it (any depth below the parent root).
3. **Case A:** open a file from the nested repo, then reload the window. The nested repo shows up as its own source-control provider.
4. **Case B:** from a clean load with no nested-repo file open, open that same file afterwards. The nested repo does **not** show up.

Same file, same repository, different result depending only on whether it was open at startup.

## Summary

Whether a **nested** git repository (one whose root sits below an already-open workspace/parent repository) gets registered depends on timing:

- If a file belonging to the nested repo is **already open when the window loads**, the nested repo appears in Source Control.
- If the **same file is opened later**, the nested repo never appears.

The behavior is inconsistent.

## Cause (from the Git extension source + trace)

`Model.doInitialScan()` in `extensions/git/src/model.ts` runs three tasks concurrently:

```js
const initialScanFn = () => Promise.all([
  this.onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders({ added: workspace.workspaceFolders || [], removed: [] }),
  this.onDidChangeVisibleTextEditors(window.visibleTextEditors),
  this.scanWorkspaceFolders()
]);
```

- **At load:** `onDidChangeVisibleTextEditors` processes files already open. For a visible file, the parent repo may not be registered yet (opening it requires spawning git), so `getRepository(uri)` returns `undefined` and `openRepository(path.dirname(uri))` is called. That resolves via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (`Git.getRepositoryRoot()` in `extensions/git/src/git.ts`) to the **nested** repo root and opens it.
- **Opened later:** the parent repo is already registered, so `getRepository(uri)` returns it and the handler short-circuits:

  ```
  [Model][onDidChangeVisibleTextEditors] Repository for editor resource
    …/<nested-repo>/<file>
    already exists: /…/<parent-repo>
  ```

  `openRepository` is never called for the nested repo.

`getRepository()` matches purely by **path ancestry** (`isDescendant` over `this.openRepositories`, deepest root first) and only considers *already-open* repositories. Once the parent is open it always shadows a not-yet-open nested repo; the only carve-out is submodules of an open repository, which does not apply to plain nested repos.

## Impact

Nested-repo detection is timing-dependent and inconsistent. In practice a nested repo can only be surfaced reliably by keeping one of its files open across reloads, or by declaring it explicitly in `git.scanRepositories`. Opening a file on demand, which works at startup, silently does nothing afterwards.

Note that Case A working at all is itself a race: the visible-editors task usually wins because opening the parent repo requires spawning a git process, but nothing guarantees the ordering.

## Request

Make open-editors detection consistent: when a file is opened, open the **deepest** repository that contains it, even if an ancestor repository is already open (or provide an opt-in setting for this). The outcome should not depend on whether the file happened to be open at startup.

## Workaround

- `git.scanRepositories` with the nested repo's path. Only paths relative to a workspace folder are accepted; absolute paths are explicitly rejected (`Model.scanWorkspaceFolders()`).
- Keeping a nested-repo file open across window reloads.

## Related issues

None of these fixed the open-editors code path described above; the short-circuit still exists on current `main` (1.131.0).

- [#133577](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/133577): umbrella feature request for nested repository detection. Closed when workspace folder scanning shipped; the openEditors gap remained.
- [#322859](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/322859): same symptom (nested repo appears only after opening a file and reloading the window). Closed by the reporter; the root cause there was the `git.repositoryScanMaxDepth` default. The reload behavior it describes is exactly the startup race explained here.
- [#198744](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/198744): same symptom (editing a nested-repo file no longer opens the repo). Turned out to be a GitLens regression and was closed by the reporter. It shows the open-on-edit behavior users expect comes from GitLens, not the built-in Git extension.
- [#189287](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/189287) (`bug`, `git`, `confirmed`, still open): a different symptom of the same root cause, purely path-based attribution in `getRepository()`, in the opposite direction. A diff for a file tracked by the ancestor repo resolves its original content against the deepest open repo, where the file is ignored, so the original side shows empty. This report is the detection/registration counterpart: there the deepest open repo wrongly wins, here the already-open ancestor wrongly wins.

title: Fix Add Feedback button layout and stretching in editor gutter #327107
body:
Fixes: #327107

## Proposed Changes

- **Moved to margin overlays.** Changed the agent feedback hover glyph from hijacking line-number rendering (`lineNumberClassName`) to injecting into the dedicated `.margin-view-overlays` band (`linesDecorationsClassName`), matching the approach used by VS Code's native comment glyphs.
- **Standardized sizing.** Replaced the `inset: 0` CSS rule — which stretched the button to fill the entire line-number container width, producing a wide rectangle in diff-editor views — with fixed-dimension constraints (`width: 18px`, `left: -6px`) consistent with existing margin glyph conventions, so the `+` icon renders as a fixed square regardless of gutter width.
- **Updated hover/accessibility target.** Switched `lineNumberHoverMessage` to `glyphMarginHoverMessage` so the "Add Feedback" tooltip attaches to the correct location now that the glyph lives in the margin overlay layer rather than the line-number column.

## How to test

- [ ] Open a workspace with an active Agent Host / Chat Session that populates feedback glyphs in the editor gutter.
- [ ] Hover the gutter to reveal the "Add Feedback" (`+`) button. Confirm it renders as a clean square and doesn't overlap the line number.
- [ ] Open a file with changes in the split diff editor, hover the gutter, and confirm the button no longer stretches into a wide rectangle.
- [ ] Set a breakpoint on the same line as an "Add Feedback" glyph and confirm the two don't visually collide in the margin.
- [ ] Tab through with keyboard only (no mouse) and confirm the "Add Feedback" tooltip announces correctly when the margin receives focus.

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
VS Code detects repositories two ways, and they treat a parent `.gitignore` **oppositely**:

| Mechanism | Setting | Honors `.gitignore`? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subfolder scan | `git.repositoryScanMaxDepth` | **No** | Finds repos in ignored folders, but bulk-adds *all* of them |
| Open-editors | `autoRepositoryDetection: openEditors` | **Yes** | On-demand per opened file, but suppressed inside ignored folders |

Because they disagree, one natural behavior is unreachable: **register a repo only when I open one of its files, even if it lives in an ignored folder.** `repositoryScanMaxDepth` bulk-adds everything; `scanRepositories` is a static hand-kept list; `openEditors` is suppressed by `.gitignore`.

This matters for repos actively developed inside a dependency/output folder the outer repo ignores (package/vendor dirs, vendored sources). Un-ignoring the folder isn't viable.

**Proposal:** a single setting applied to **both** mechanisms:

```jsonc
"git.detectRepositoriesInIgnoredFolders": false // default = current behavior
```

When `true`, neither the scan nor open-editors is suppressed by a parent `.gitignore`. Folder exclusions stay controlled by the explicit `git.repositoryScanIgnoredFolders` list.

Related: #41565 — its fix covered the scan-depth path only; the on-demand/open-editors case inside ignored folders is the gap here.

title: Agents: let agents manage automations
body:
## Summary

Adds an Agents-window **Automations** client-tool set so agents can list, create, update, and delete scheduled automations without bypassing the user’s existing tool approval policy.

- `listAutomations` returns stable IDs, editable fields, targets, and timing metadata.
- `configureAutomation` creates or partially updates an automation. It **never opens the automation Create/Edit dialog**: calls requiring interaction use normal tool confirmation, while centrally auto-approved calls proceed directly. Both paths run the same validation and guarded mutation.
- `deleteAutomation` follows normal approval policy. Interactive calls show **Delete**/**Cancel**; centrally auto-approved calls delete without a custom-button value.
- Successful create/update calls render a secondary chat button such as **Created an automation: Morning review** or **Edited an automation: Morning review**. Activating it opens Customizations → Automations and expands, reveals, and focuses the affected stable ID.
- All writes continue through `IAutomationService`; tools never write storage directly.

The PR also makes the existing shared automation snapshot safe under concurrent window mutations. It does **not** add or migrate a database schema.

## Suggested review order

| Order | Area | Primary files | Verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tool behavior | `src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/browser/automationTools.ts` | Strict input parsing, current-session targets, standard confirmation metadata, direct create/update, Delete/Cancel semantics |
| 2 | Conflict safety | common + Sessions `automationService.ts` | One canonical editable-state definition, preparation→approval conflict detection, final guarded update, runtime metadata tolerance |
| 3 | Result UI | `chatService.ts`, `chatToolInvocation.ts`, `chatAutomationConfiguredResultSubPart.ts`, `chatToolInvocationPart.ts` | Success-only structured data, deterministic pill, keyboard-accessible button |
| 4 | Navigation + restore | AI Customization editor/list files; `stateToProgressAdapter.ts` | Open Automations, focus stable ID, live and restored Agent Host result reconstruction |
| 5 | Agent Host approval bridge | `copilotAgentSession.ts`, `agentHostSessionHandler.ts` | Allow all stamps setting-driven approval on direct client-tool-ready calls; local tool confirmation is skipped |
| 6 | Removed complexity | automation dialog contract/implementation, `chatInputPart.ts`, tools service | No agent-proposal dialog branch; no generic `confirmationReason` plumbing; manual dialog remains intact |
| 7 | Persistence | automation storage services, storage IPC, browser IndexedDB storage | Authoritative single-key CAS, retry/rebase, no unrelated-key writes or schema migration |

The focused test files mirror these layers; `automationTools.test.ts` is the best behavior-level starting point.

## Approval behavior

| Operation | Interaction required by current policy | Centrally auto-approved |
|---|---|---|
| List | Executes immediately | Executes immediately |
| Create/update | Shows normal tool confirmation, then validates and persists | Validates and persists directly |
| Delete | Shows Delete/Cancel confirmation | Deletes directly |

`LanguageModelToolsService` remains the sole workbench approval authority after hooks, enterprise restrictions, session permission level, per-tool settings, Agent Host preapproval, and Autopilot risk assessment. Automation code does not re-read or reinterpret those settings.

For Copilot Agent Host sessions, SDK **Allow all** mode directly readies client tools instead of producing a provider permission request. The ready action now carries `autoApproveBySetting`, allowing the existing Agent Host→workbench bridge to pass `preApproved` and avoid a second local confirmation. A plain protocol `not-needed` reason is deliberately not treated as setting approval because default-ready client tools can use the same reason.

Denial happens before `invoke`; cancellation, disabled Automations, invalid IDs/targets, and conflicts return without writing. Explicit targets must resolve through the live workspace or quick-chat session-type catalogs. Omitted or `currentSession` targets use the invoking Agents session.

## Update safety

There are two intentionally separate conflict boundaries:

1. `prepareToolInvocation` records the automation’s canonical editable state in transient preparation data. After approval, `invoke` re-reads the automation and rejects editable changes made while confirmation was pending. This data is omitted from serialized chat invocations.
2. `updateAutomationIfUnchanged` compares the same canonical editable state inside the authoritative ledger mutation. The storage CAS/retry loop closes the final invoke→persist race.

Runtime-only `updatedAt`, `lastRunAt`, and `nextRunAt` changes do not conflict, so scheduler progress is preserved. Editable changes fail closed and require `listAutomations` to refresh.

## Chat result flow

- Native live calls propagate `IToolResult.toolSpecificData` into `ChatToolInvocation` after a successful mutation.
- Native serialized chat keeps the structured `automationConfigured` result.
- Agent Host live completion attaches the same data in `finalizeToolInvocation`.
- Agent Host history reconstructs it from the successful `configureAutomation` JSON result, matching the existing `sessionCreated` pattern.
- Errors and cancellation never produce `automationConfigured`, so they cannot render a false success button.

The button reuses the existing quiet secondary result treatment, uses `Codicon.watch`, exposes localized visible/title text, and is fully keyboard operable.

## Persistence and corruption boundaries

The subsystem already stores definitions and retained run history together under application-scope key `chat.automations.ledger`. This PR retains that versioned snapshot.

Every mutation now performs:

1. authoritative raw read;
2. parse + record-scoped mutation;
3. retained-run trimming;
4. compare-and-swap of the exact old ledger value to revision + 1;
5. re-read and reapply on contention.

Desktop linearizes the comparison in the main-process storage channel. Web uses one IndexedDB `readwrite` transaction against the existing application database/fallback. Both paths touch only the automation key.

Safety invariants:

- no table, object-store, IndexedDB-version, or ledger-schema migration;
- no direct tool storage writes;
- no stale full-snapshot overwrite across windows;
- no unrelated-key enumeration, replacement, or deletion;
- no future-schema downgrade;
- automation deletion removes retained runs atomically while already-dispatched sessions continue independently.

## Manual dialog behavior

Agent configure calls no longer use the dialog. Manual Create/Edit still does. The independently useful behavior that automation workspace choices do not update new-session recents remains.

The final safety review found one manual-dialog cold-start race: late discovery of a saved custom mode could overwrite a mode the user selected while waiting. The retry now fails closed when the current mode has changed.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run precommit`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused Electron suites for automation tools/service/dialog/runner/scheduler, central approval resolution, Copilot Agent Host client-tool permission propagation, Agent Host state conversion/client tools, chat result routing/accessibility, Automations list navigation, storage IPC/IndexedDB, and tool-set registration
- Two independent Claude Opus 4.8 long-context/max-reasoning reviews: bug/safety and architecture/overengineering. The single valid finding (manual mode retry race) is addressed; no blocking architecture or data-loss findings remain.

## Out of scope

- Changing scheduler cadence or leadership behavior
- Stopping an already-dispatched session when its automation is deleted
- Migrating persistence to per-record keys or a new database schema

body:
### Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?

No. The failure is in Copilot Chat MCP tool dispatch.

### VS Code Version

1.129.1\ncommit 8a7abeba6e03ea3af87bfbce9a1b7e48fed567b8\nLinux x64

### Reproduction

1. Configure a valid stdio MCP server in User `mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "nebuCtx": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "nebu-ctx",
      "args": []
    }
  }
}
```

2. The server initializes using MCP protocol `2025-06-18` and publishes valid object input schemas for four tools.
3. Start a new GitHub Copilot Chat agent session whose first response invokes one or more of those MCP tools.

### Actual

The first calls in a new chat intermittently fail before the stdio server receives JSON-RPC:

```text
Error from tool mcp_nebu-ctx_ctx with args ...: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading `invoke`)
    at AF.invokeTool (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:3412:12541)
    at async wBt.$invokeTool (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:1021:96995)
```

When it happens, several independently requested MCP tools fail in the same 2 ms window. The issue is only observed in VS Code/Copilot; the same server works through its CLI client.

A direct stdio probe succeeds: `initialize` succeeds, `tools/list` returns all four tools, and server stderr is empty. The schemas use only valid `object`, `properties`, `required`, primitive types, and array `items`. VS Code itself had already started its Copilot CLI MCP service more than two minutes before the failed first-call batch, so this appears to be a per-chat deferred-tool adapter registration/lookup race rather than child-process startup.

### Expected

Copilot should not advertise/invoke an MCP tool until its adapter is registered. If lookup occurs while registration is pending, resolve/await registration or retry the lookup rather than dereferencing an undefined adapter.

### Notes

The nebu-ctx report with supporting evidence is https://github.com/MarkBovee/nebu-ctx/issues/29.

title: AgentHost: fall back to Auto when a selected Copilot CLI model is unavailable
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This is a **potential fix** based on a telemetry investigation, not a confirmed
> root-cause fix. This PR description was written by GitHub Copilot, and the commit is
> co-authored by Copilot. Please review the reasoning critically before merging.

## Problem

During the AHP stable rollout (`ahp-both-windows`, 25% stage), **Copilot CLI on the Agent Host**
(`sessiontype = agent-host-copilotcli`) shows roughly **2× the request error rate** of Copilot CLI on
the Extension Host (`copilotcli`). Claude on Agent Host is at parity-or-better, so this is specific to
the Copilot CLI model path, not the Agent Host generally.

The regression is concentrated in **model selection**. Comparing the two harnesses by model class and
looking at the full **success rate** (not just error rate):

| Model class | AH success% | EH success% | note |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| auto | 86.3 | 87.1 | ~parity |
| named (claude-*, gpt-*, …) | 87.0 | 87.6 | ~parity |
| **path-like (BYOK/Ollama/custom)** | **51.0** | **87.5** | **the regression** |
| empty (no resolvable model) | 34.4 | 29.5 | bad on both |

The standout is **path-like model ids** (BYOK/Ollama/custom models such as
`ollama/qwen2.5-coder:latest`, `provider/model:7b`): they are **~38× more prevalent on the Agent Host
picker** than on the Extension Host and drop from ~88% to ~51% success. These are selectable on the AH
Copilot-CLI picker (the harness publishes its own model list, including bridged renderer BYOK models),
whereas the EH `copilotcli` picker never offered them. This is **causally isolated**: within the same
ExP cohort — and even for the *same* treatment-cohort users — path-like models succeed on EH but fail
on AH, and a separate harness-side event (`agenthost.turncompleted`, un-redacted model) reproduces the
same 51% / 88% split.

Two code facts make an unavailable/stale selection fail hard instead of degrading gracefully:

1. The AH send path forwards the remembered model id **raw** to the harness/SDK with no
   validate-and-fallback step (`baseAgentHostSessionsProvider` → `copilotSessionLauncher`).
2. The restore path was recently changed (#326938) to keep a remembered agent-host selection
   `pending` (wait for the async model list) instead of falling back to Auto — which is correct for
   restore, but means a genuinely-unavailable selection can still be *sent*.

The Copilot SDK then throws on an unroutable model id rather than falling back to Auto, so the whole
turn errors.

## What this PR does

Adds a small **send-time** validation in `BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider`. Before dispatching a
request, `_resolveSendModelId(...)` resolves the selected model against the session's available
models (`getModelsSnapshot`). If the selection is **conclusively `unavailable`** *and* the harness
supports Auto, it drops the selection so the request falls back to the harness default/Auto instead
of erroring on a model id the harness cannot route. It is applied in both send paths
(`_sendCommittedChatRequest` and `_sendNewSessionRequest`).

This intentionally mirrors the model picker's own removed-model fallback, applying it at send time
where an unavailable selection is authoritative (the restore-time `pending` grace from #326938 is
preserved — `pending` selections are left untouched). Sessions that require an explicit model and do
**not** support Auto (e.g. Copilot Free/Student Claude) keep their selection, so the existing "no
models available" UX is unchanged.

## ⚠️ Product caveat (BYOK → Auto)

For a *deliberately-chosen* BYOK/Ollama model, silently redirecting to Copilot's cloud `auto` defeats
the user's local/privacy intent and sends their prompt to the cloud. This guard only fires when the
selection is **conclusively unavailable** (the request would otherwise fail), so it trades a hard
failure for a cloud fallback — but reviewers should decide whether a **clear, actionable error** (or a
hardened BYOK bridge) is preferable to Auto for BYOK selections. Note BYOK-on-AH is currently
experimental (remote unsupported per #325738; local behind `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`).

## Scope / expected impact

- Targets the **path-like/BYOK and stale-selection** slice — the clearest, causally-isolated
  regression (~715 devices). Together with the `empty` bucket this is ~57% of AH Copilot-CLI errors.
- `named`/`auto` models are **at success parity** AH vs EH (~87% each), so they are **not** the target
  and not meaningfully regressed. (This corrects an earlier framing that described a "broad degradation
  of all models" — the total-error increase there is mostly offset by fewer cancellations.)
- Only partially helps the `empty`-model bucket (no resolvable model / not-authed / model-list-not-
  ready) and does **not** address BYOK-bridge *inference* failures (where a model resolves but the
  renderer↔node↔loopback bridge fails mid-stream, ~1/3 of path-like failures).

## Testing

- ESLint clean; type-checks locally.
- ⚠️ No automated test added yet and this has not been validated against live sessions — it is a
  proposed mitigation. Suggested validation: confirm the AH `copilotcli` success rate for the
  path-like model bucket improves without regressing sessions that legitimately use Auto or a valid
  explicit model.

## Analysis reference & caveats

- Regression is a property of the harness (`sessiontype`), not the ExP cohort; present within every
  VS Code build (rules out a version confound); appeared only when the 25% ramp routed the general
  population onto the Agent Host path.
- **Data limitation:** there is no direct error-category telemetry for the regression period — the
  `errorType`/`modelSelectionKind` fields are on `agenthost.turncompleted` (not

title: Feature Request: Allow specifying reasoning effort per subagent invocation
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Currently, the `runSubagent` tool (used by chat agents / extensions to delegate tasks to sub-agents) does not expose a parameter to control the **reasoning effort** (thinking budget) of the spawned subagent. The only way to influence reasoning effort is through the global session-level setting or the upcoming "efficiency mode" toggle (#320470).

This is insufficient for real-world orchestration scenarios where a single session spawns multiple subagents with **very different complexity requirements**:

| Task delegated to subagent | Ideal effort |
|---|---|
| Simple file search / grep | `low` |
| One-shot code generation from a known pattern | `low` or `medium` |
| Complex multi-step analysis or architecture decision | `high` |
| Research across multiple files with synthesis | `high` |

A global toggle forces an all-or-nothing trade-off — either all subagents burn maximum tokens, or all are constrained.

## Proposed Solution

Allow specifying reasoning effort **per subagent call**, with two complementary surfaces:

### Option A: `reasoningEffort` parameter on the `runSubagent` tool

```jsonc
{
  "prompt": "...",
  "model": "Claude Opus 4.6 (copilot)",
  "reasoningEffort": "high"   // "high" | "medium" | "low"
}
```

This gives the orchestrating agent (or extension) dynamic, per-call control.

### Option B: Declarative default in `.agent.md` frontmatter

```yaml
---
tools: [...]
reasoningEffort: low
---
```

This lets agent authors set a sensible default for their agent's typical workload, while still allowing per-call override via Option A.

## Benefits

- **Cost optimization**: Low-effort subagents for trivial lookups save significant tokens/credits without degrading quality on complex tasks.
- **Latency**: Lower effort → faster responses for simple delegations.
- **Composability**: Power users and extension authors can build efficient multi-agent workflows with fine-grained control.
- **Complementary to #320470**: The global efficiency mode sets a floor; per-subagent effort allows targeted overrides.

## Related

- #320470 — Explore an "efficiency mode" selection for chat (mentions "low reasoning for subagents" as part of global mode)

title: Feature Request: Allow filtering/hiding chat sessions by specific agent/provider
body:
## Summary

Currently, when multiple agent providers (Copilot, Claude, Codex, etc.) are active, their chat sessions are all merged into the same session list (Chat view / Agent Sessions), with no way to hide sessions from one specific provider while keeping others visible.

## Use Case

I use Claude Code and the OpenAI Codex extension side by side in VS Code. I want to:
- Keep using the Codex extension for occasional tasks (via its own panel/sidebar)
- Prevent Codex's sessions from cluttering the main Chat view / session list, which I primarily use for Claude/Copilot sessions

Currently there is no setting to achieve this. Related attempts that don't fully work:
- `chat.agentHost.enabled: false` doesn't fully hide sessions from that provider (see #318836)
- Archiving/deleting sessions only clears existing history; new sessions from the unwanted provider still appear afterward
- Dragging a provider's tab out to its own sidebar panel (as a workaround) doesn't stop its sessions from also appearing in the main Chat view's session list

This is somewhat related to #277696, which asks that hidden agents remain usable — my request is the session-list equivalent: let a provider still be fully usable (via its own panel), while excluding its sessions from the shared/merged session list.

## Proposed Solution

Add a setting (or per-provider context menu action in the sessions list) to exclude a specific agent/provider's sessions from the merged Chat view / Agent Sessions list, without disabling the provider or preventing it from being used elsewhere (e.g. its own dedicated panel).

Example:
```jsonc
"chat.agentSessions.excludedProviders": ["openai.codex"]
```

## Related Issues
- #318836 (chat.agentHost.enabled doesn't hide remote sessions)
- #277696 (hidden agents become unusable)
- #282607 (Hide Agent Sessions Sidebar doesn't work)

title: Stream built-in shell output over AHP terminal channel
body:
Related: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/352
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324825
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/323399

Adopts the terminal completion model from microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352 and supersedes the cumulative-Text approach from #326291.

- Re-vendor the pending AHP contract: remove `terminalComplete`, move `exitCode`/`preview`/`truncated` onto the terminal block as `result`, and add `isPty` to terminal tool results and terminal state.
- Stream public Copilot SDK `tool.execution_partial_result` events into output-only AHP terminal channels for runtime-executed shell tools, while leaving client-hosted PTY terminals on their existing path.
- Treat partial output as cumulative runtime snapshots: append only the unseen suffix while the snapshot grows, then clear and replay it when truncation rewrites the snapshot.
- Create the output channel before publishing its terminal block, including commands with no partial events; seed final preview data, persist the exit result, and keep background channels open until `shell_completed` supplies the real exit code.
- Attach non-PTY channels to chat through a read-only output source without creating an `ITerminalInstance`, adding a root terminal entry, opening a bottom-panel terminal, or exposing terminal Focus/Show actions.
- Render plain-text output in the existing detached xterm, normalize LF to CRLF only in the Agent Host output adapter, and serialize append/reset writes so streaming output is neither duplicated nor stale.
- Preserve live auto-expansion and running/completed command decorations for output-only tools while leaving the existing PTY decoration path unchanged.
- Reconstruct history with a stable non-PTY terminal URI and structured result, while retaining a structural fallback for old persisted `terminalComplete` blocks.
- Re-apply the local `CompletionItem.label` extension from #326807 after protocol generation. The generated snapshot still needs a final `.ahp-version` sync after microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352 lands.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The `isPty` and `result: TerminalCommandResult` shapes come from the protocol change itself: [`ToolResultTerminalContent`/`TerminalCommandResult`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-chat/state.ts#L1398-L1432) and [`TerminalState.isPty`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-terminal/state.ts#L110-L116).
- The attach-once terminal-block policy extends the existing PTY completion deduplication in [`copilotAgentSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3293-L3304).
- Updating terminal state before dispatching data, so late subscribers can reconstruct output from the snapshot, follows [`AgentHostTerminalManager._handlePtyData`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L608-L638).
- The output-only channel URI follows the existing Agent Host shell namespace in [`copilotShellTools`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotShellTools.ts#L172-L179).
- Output-only auto-expansion reuses the command lifecycle semantics already used by the AHP terminal path in [`ChatTerminalToolProgressPart._attachAhpCommandSource`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L926-L987).

title: gate nonpty terminal actions
body:
Summary
Fixes the inline terminal preview offering "Focus/Show Terminal" and a "view stale terminal" action for non-pty (SDK built-in / streaming) shell runs, where there is no real interactive terminal to focus.

The bug
The chat terminal preview (ChatTerminalToolProgressPart) decides whether to show the Focus/Show-Terminal action purely from whether a terminal instance exists (_toolbarHasInstance = !!terminalInstance), and its "open the terminal" fallback calls terminalService.openResource(terminalCommandUri). Neither has any notion of whether that terminal is a real interactive pty or an output-only, non-pty channel.

That distinction started to matter with the shell-output-streaming work (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067): to stream output, a non-pty SDK shell run now emits a Terminal content block (agenthost-terminal://shell/copilotNonPtyShells/{toolCallId}, isPty: false). The adapter sets terminalToolSessionId for any Terminal block with no isPty guard, so a non-pty run now gets a terminalToolSessionId → a revived ITerminalInstance → _toolbarHasInstance === true → the Focus/Show action and the stale openResource fallback render. But these terminals are output-only: there is nothing interactive to focus, and "opening" them just surfaces an empty/stale terminal.

The protocol already carries the needed signal — isPty on ToolResultTerminalContent / TerminalState — but it was only consumed on the host side (agentHostPty uses it to set convertEol). It never reached IChatTerminalToolInvocationData, and the widget never gated any UI on it.

Approach
Propagate the existing isPty signal end-to-end to the renderer, and gate the instance-dependent affordances on it — rather than inventing a new heuristic in the UI. Output-only non-pty terminals keep their preview (command, decoration, streamed output) but drop the actions that only make sense for a real interactive pty.

Changes and why
stateToProgressAdapter.ts (buildTerminalToolSpecificData) and agentHostSessionHandler.ts (_reviveTerminalIfNeeded) — read isPty off the Terminal content block and carry it onto the invocation data, in both producers, via a shared getTerminalContentIsPty helper.
Why: the terminal payload is built in two places — the main builder (create / streaming refresh / finalize / history replay) and the async terminal-revive path — so both must set the flag for it to stay consistent across every lifecycle stage. ?? existing preserves it across streaming refreshes.

chatService.ts (IChatTerminalToolInvocationData) — add the isPty field.
Why: the renderer had no channel to learn a terminal was non-pty; this is the missing carrier.

chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts — add a single _isNonPtyTerminal (isPty === false) check and use it to hide the Focus/Show Terminal action and early-return focusTerminal() for non-pty terminals. The early-return covers every caller — the toolbar button, the "Focus Most Recent Terminal" command, and the collapsible "Show" link — including the stale openResource(terminalCommandUri) fallback.
Why: for output-only non-pty terminals there is no interactive session to focus; showing the action or opening a stale/empty terminal is misleading. The command decoration and streamed output are unaffected — only the interactive affordances are withheld.

stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts — assert isPty is threaded from the block (false / true / unset) and that it survives a streaming-output refresh (the revive → refresh race).

Notes / not in scope
Command decoration and output streaming for these runs are handled by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067 (exit code now lives on the terminal block result; output streams via the non-pty channel). This PR only removes the incorrect interactive affordances.
The isPty semantics match the protocol flag added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067: false = output-only non-pty channel; true/absent = pty-backed (custom-terminal or local) — those keep Focus/Show.
Known gap / follow-up
The isPty data-threading is unit-tested, but the widget gating behavior itself — Focus/Show hidden and focusTerminal() a no-op for non-pty cards — has no direct test. ChatTerminalToolProgressPart is never constructed in the test suite, and doing so needs substantial service/DOM mock setup, so it was left as a follow-up rather than done here. title: git: skip textconv for quick-diff originals (#113609)

Fixes #113609

## Summary
- Quick-diff originals are read via the `git:` FS provider → `Repository.buffer()` → `git show --textconv`, so a global `diff.*.textconv` filter can change the "original" while the editor shows the raw working tree.

title: Opening a non-existent file should not trigger "save dirty file"  (Vim/Emacs-style "nothing changed, nothing to save")

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

milestone.title: Backlog Candidates
milestone.description: Work that is not yet accepted for the Backlog. We wait for the community to weigh in.

body:
## Feature request

Add a setting that prevents a newly created, **empty and untouched** file from being treated as "dirty," so that closing it does not trigger a "Do you want to save?" prompt.

In Microsoft VSCode, if you open a new file ("code doesnotexist.txt` from the Terminal), make no changes, then try to exit, it asks if you want to save the file. Other editors, such as Vim and Emacs, do not ask to save the file. The logic of Vim and Emacs is that no changes (including creating the file) have happened, therefore there is nothing to save.

I'm requesting a feature to enable the behavior that Vim/Emacs uses.

## Current behavior

When you create a new file that has an associated path (for example `code newfile.txt` on a not-yet-existing file, or `File > New File‚` where you name it before it exists on disk), VSCode marks the editor as dirty **immediately**, before you type anything. Trying to close or exit then prompts you to save  even though you made no changes and the file is empty.

> **Note:** A plain `File > New Untitled Text File` / `Ctrl+N` with no path does *not* have this problem -- it only becomes dirty once you type. This request is specifically about new files that carry an associated file path.

## Expected / desired behavior

Optionally match the behavior of editors like Vim and Emacs: if you create a new file, make no changes, and then quit, nothing was modified -- so there is nothing to save and no prompt should appear. The file should simply not be created on disk. As soon as you type any content, normal dirty-tracking and the save prompt would resume.

I'd propose an opt-in setting, e.g.:

```jsonc
// Whether a newly created empty file with an associated path is considered
// unsaved. When false, an untouched new file closes without a save prompt
// and is not written to disk (Vim/Emacs behavior).
"workbench.editor.untitled.dirtyWhenEmpty": true  // default preserves today's behavior
```

Why?

Users coming from Vim/Emacs (and terminal-centric workflows) find the current prompt surprising: they opened a path, decided not to use it, and expect quitting to be a no-op. The reasoning "no changes were made, therefore there is nothing to save" is a well-established convention.

Notes on scope

This looks like a small, localized change. The dirty state for these editors is initialized in untitledTextEditorModel.ts (this.dirty = this.hasAssociatedFilePath || !!this.initialValue;), and there's already an "empty content / not dirty" path that is currently skipped when the editor has an associated file path. A setting could gate that behavior. Restored hot-exit backups should presumably remain dirty regardless, since they represent real unsaved content.

title: sessions: fix Agents window hang with per-group editor limit of 1
body:
Fixes #327066

## What

Enforce `showTabs: 'multiple'` and `limit: { enabled: false }` on the single-pane editor part (`SinglePaneMainEditorPart`) via the existing `enforcePartOptions` API.

## Why

The single-pane docked tab bar keeps several managed editors open at once — the pinned Changes multi-diff tab, the Files placeholder, and any real file tabs (`[Changes][Files][file…]`). Two user settings break this layout:

- `workbench.editor.showTabs` set to `single`/`none` collapses the docked tab strip.
- `workbench.editor.limit` (especially `perEditorGroup: true, value: 1`) makes `EditorsObserver` auto-evict the least-recently-used tab. Since the managed tabs are pinned (not sticky), they get evicted, the managed-tab reconciliation reopens them, and the observer evicts again — an infinite open/close loop that hangs the renderer (the reported bug).

## Notes for reviewers

- Scoped to the single-pane editor part only; the user's `workbench.editor.showTabs` / `workbench.editor.limit` settings are untouched everywhere else.
- `limit: { enabled: false }` is sufficient because `EditorsObserver.ensureOpenedEditorsLimit` returns early when the limit is disabled, so the other limit fields are never read.
- The `showTabs` enforcement was already present; this PR adds the `limit` enforcement to close the hang.

Replaces the two independent mic buttons in the chat input with a **single segmented control** that unifies Dictation and live Voice Mode, and adds **two selectable Voice Mode interaction styles** to compare. Everything is gated behind experimental settings and defaults off.

### Why
Watching people use Voice Mode for the first time, a recurring problem was ending up in *both* dictation and voice at once, and confusion about which button connects vs. toggles listening vs. disconnects. This unifies the two into one discoverable control with clear animated state feedback, and mutual exclusion so you can only be in one mode at a time.

- `chat.voiceInputMode.segmentedToggle` (boolean, default `false`) — show the single segmented control instead of the two separate mic buttons.
- `chat.voiceInputMode.interactionStyle` (`holdToTalk` | `listenButton`, default `holdToTalk`) — how Voice Mode drives listening.

### The two interaction styles
1. **`holdToTalk`** — the voice button is push-to-talk: **hold** it (or the `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Space` keybinding) to talk, release to send; a **quick tap** turns Voice Mode off.
2. **`listenButton`** — the voice button is a **power toggle** (connect / disconnect, and starts listening on connect); a **separate person-voice button** toggles listening on and off in manual mode.

### Highlights
- Dictation and Voice Mode live in one constant-size housing; icons slide/collapse between states.
- Voice Mode renders as an animated **Device EQ waveform** that transforms by state: idle undulating wave, **blue** mic-reactive listening, **purple** TTS-reactive speaking, and a short "silent" hover preview for disconnect — colors match the input-box glow.
- **Fix:** live Voice Mode previously cut off after ~one word. `pttDown`/`pttUp` now take a `force` flag so hold-to-talk records a clean turn and finishes on release, bypassing the short-tap toggle mode and the auto-send silence timer.

title: Stream built-in shell output over AHP terminal channel
body:
Related: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/352
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324825
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/323399

- Adopt the terminal completion model from microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352: move command `exitCode`/`preview`/`truncated` onto the terminal result and distinguish PTY-backed terminals from plain-text output channels with `isPty`.
- Stream public Copilot SDK `tool.execution_partial_result` events from runtime-executed shell tools into output-only AHP terminal channels, while keeping client-hosted PTY terminals on their existing path.
- Treat partial output as cumulative runtime snapshots: append only the unseen suffix while a snapshot grows, then clear and replay it when runtime truncation rewrites the snapshot.
- Create an output channel on the first partial result or when foreground shell completion supplies retained output or exit metadata. Leave background shell handoff and completions with neither output nor exit metadata out of the inline terminal path.
- Prefer structured SDK `shell_exit` metadata for the command result. When the external SDK bridge removes that block, use the runtime's trailing shell-completion marker as a scoped non-PTY fallback for the exit code and retained preview.
- Attach output-only channels to chat through a read-only output source without creating an `ITerminalInstance`, adding a root terminal entry, opening a panel terminal, or exposing terminal Focus/Show actions.
- Render the plain-text stream in the existing detached xterm, normalize line endings only in the Agent Host output adapter, and serialize snapshot writes so growing or rewritten output is not duplicated or stale.
- Preserve live auto-expansion and running/completed decorations for output-only tools. Existing Local harness and Agent Host PTY terminal behavior remain on the original path unless `isPty === false`.
- Scope output-channel URIs by Agent Host session and tool call, and reconstruct completed history from the terminal's structured result.
- Re-vendor the generated protocol snapshot after microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352 lands and use its final commit for `.ahp-version`.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The `isPty` and `result: TerminalCommandResult` shapes come from the protocol change itself: [`ToolResultTerminalContent`/`TerminalCommandResult`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-chat/state.ts#L1398-L1432) and [`TerminalState.isPty`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-terminal/state.ts#L110-L116).
- Publishing a terminal block once extends the existing PTY completion deduplication in [`copilotAgentSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3293-L3304).
- Updating terminal state before dispatching data, so late subscribers can reconstruct output from the snapshot, follows [`AgentHostTerminalManager._handlePtyData`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L608-L638).
- The output-only channel URI follows the existing Agent Host shell namespace in [`copilotShellTools`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotShellTools.ts#L172-L179).
- Output-only auto-expansion reuses the command lifecycle semantics already used by the AHP terminal path in [`ChatTerminalToolProgressPart._attachAhpCommandSource`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L926-L987).

body:
## Summary

The Agents window can enter an infinite editor open/close loop when the editor limit is enabled per group with a value of 1. The renderer main thread remains busy and the UI hangs.

## Configuration

```json
"workbench.editor.limit.perEditorGroup": true,
"workbench.editor.limit.value": 1,
"workbench.editor.limit.enabled": true
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Apply the settings above.
2. Open the Agents window.
3. Open a workspace-backed session that uses the single-pane layout and has the managed Changes and Files tabs.

## Actual behavior

The UI hangs. The managed Changes and Files tabs continuously displace one another:

1. `SinglePaneManagedTabsStrategy` ensures both managed tabs.
2. Opening the second tab triggers `EditorsObserver.ensureOpenedEditorsLimit`, which evicts the least-recent tab because the per-group limit is 1.
3. The managed-tab editor-change observer sees the missing tab and reopens it.
4. The editor limit evicts the other managed tab, and the cycle repeats indefinitely.

## Expected behavior

The managed-tab reconciliation and editor-limit enforcement should reach a stable state. Enabling an editor limit of 1 must not cause an infinite open/close loop or hang the renderer.

## Trace evidence

- Renderer PID 20337 entered a `RunTask` at 9.185832 seconds after a mouse-release/session-open action.
- The task was still unfinished when the 71.9-second trace ended, after remaining open for at least 62.733 seconds.
- CPU samples repeatedly alternate between:
  - `SinglePaneManagedTabsStrategy._reconcileCore -> _openChangesTab/_openFilesTab`
  - `EditorsObserver.ensureOpenedEditorsLimit -> doEnsureOpenedEditorsLimit -> closeEditors`
- The renderer main thread is effectively continuously active from approximately 9.3 seconds onward.

## Introducing commit

`5cfa71584e11bc0fe673686a9306c285fb4956cd` — sessions: refine the single-pane detail-panel layout (#324348)

That commit first introduced the auto-managed Changes and Files tabs together with reconciliation on editor changes. Its parent does not contain the managed Files-tab reconciler; subsequent refactors preserve the conflicting invariant.

## Summary

A Git operation that requires credentials fails when its interactive credential flow runs in the sandbox. Git Credential Manager attempts to start its Avalonia-based macOS UI, but Avalonia cannot start the native render timer and aborts. Subsequent credential and askpass fallbacks also fail, leaving Git without valid credentials.

## What happened

The credential request produced the following sequence:

- Avalonia threw `System.InvalidOperationException: Avalonia.Native was not able to start the RenderTimer. Native error code is: -6661` while initializing the Git Credential Manager UI.
- `git-credential-manager get` terminated with signal 6.
- A fallback attempted to create a temporary file under macOS's `/var/folders/.../T` directory and failed with `Operation not permitted`.
- An Electron credential/askpass path reported a macOS `SecCodeCheckValidity` error.
- The operation ended with `Missing or invalid credentials` and `Missing pipe`.

The `-6661` value corresponds to CoreVideo's invalid-argument error and occurs when Avalonia cannot create a display render timer, such as when no usable active display is available in a headless, sleeping-display, remote, VM, or restricted sandbox context. Although the sandbox command sets `TMPDIR`, the failing macOS-side helper uses its own process environment and macOS temporary directory.

title: Git extension logs expected ENOENT for common refs in linked worktrees
body:
### Type of issue
Bug

### VS Code version
1.129.1 (commit 8a7abeba6e03ea3af87bfbce9a1b7e48fed567b8)

### Reproduction
1. Open a repository linked worktree in VS Code.
2. Let the Git extension resolve a remote-tracking ref such as refs/remotes/origin/dev.
3. Inspect the Git output/log.

### Actual behavior
Git.revParse first reads path.join(this.dotGit.path, ref). For a linked worktree, this points below the private per-worktree gitdir. Normal refs live below GIT_COMMON_DIR, so the speculative read raises ENOENT and logs:

[Git][revParse] Unable to read file: ENOENT ... refs/remotes/origin/dev

The subsequent git rev-parse fallback succeeds. This makes a valid repository look unhealthy and repeats for every affected ref.

### Expected behavior
Expected ENOENT from the speculative direct read should be silent. Other filesystem errors should still be logged, and the existing git rev-parse fallback should remain unchanged.

### Source
extensions/git/src/git.ts, Git.revParse: the catch currently logs every readFile error before falling back to git rev-parse.

### Proposed narrow fix
In that catch, skip the warning only when err.code === ENOENT. Keep the warning for all other errors and keep the existing fallback.

Git documents that refs are shared through the common directory for linked worktrees:
- https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree
- https://git-scm.com/docs/gitrepository-layout.html#Documentation/gitrepository-layout.txt-codeGITCOMMONDIRcode

title: Avoid :has() selectors that trigger workbench-wide style invalidation
body:
Fixes #327048

A `:has()` whose anchor exists in the live DOM makes every DOM mutation, including the inline `letter-spacing` writes the editor performs on each layout, pay a style recalc that scales with the whole visible workbench (measurements and per-rule profiling in the issue). The single biggest offender is the chat working set scrollbar rule; the root-anchored rules in floatingPanels.css and sessionsPolicyBlocked.css are the same hazard and the same class of problem that #324986 already fixed for the automations dialog.

Changes:

- `chat.css`: the working set scrollbar padding is keyed off an `overflowing` class toggled in `chatInputPart.ts`, which already computes the overflow condition (`allEntries.length > maxItemsShown`), instead of `:has(.visible.scrollbar.vertical)`. Behavior note: the padding now applies whenever the list overflows, not only while the auto-hide scrollbar is faded in. This also stops the labels from shifting under the scrollbar mid-scroll.
- `floatingPanels.css`: the two root-anchored `:has()` rules are replaced by `activitybar-compact` (mirrored onto the workbench root by `activitybarPart.ts`) and `noactivitybar` (toggled by `layout.ts` like the other part visibility classes). A `:not(.noactivitybar)` on the compact rule keeps the hidden+compact case resolving to the hidden inset, matching the specificity behavior of the old rules.
- `sessionsPolicyBlocked.css`: `.monaco-workbench:has(.sessions-policy-blocked-overlay)` becomes a class toggled for the overlay's lifetime.
- `build/stylelint.ts`: new check that errors on `:has()` anchored to a root compound (`body` / `html` / `:root` / `.monaco-workbench`), with a `stylelint-disable has-anchor-checker` escape. It flags all three historical instances (including the original #324985 one) and has no hits on current `src/**/*.css`.

Testing:

- Runtime equivalent of this change (deleting the offending rules from CSSOM plus one full restyle) takes the forced-recalc microbenchmark from 13-16ms to 0.04ms on my machine and makes sash dragging smooth again; details in the issue.
- Verified sash dragging, working set overflow padding (7+ files in the working set), compact/hidden activity bar insets under floating panels, in a local dev build.
- Lint check verified against the three historical bad selectors (all flagged) and a full run over `src/**/*.css` (no findings).

Get a chat working set populated: run an agent/edit session that changes several files, so the changed-files list (`.chat-editing-session-list`) exists in the chat input area 2. Open a few files split into 3-4 editor groups 3. Drag the sash between two editor groups, or between the editor area and a sidebar The renderer main thread pegs one core and the whole UI drops to a few fps. The more editor groups, the worse; dragging the editor/sidebar boundary (which relayouts all groups at once) is the worst case. Stable on the same machine is completely fine, and so is an insiders window without a populated working set - the reason is below. Reproduces with both `--ozone-platform=wayland` and x11, NVIDIA driver 610.43.03, hardware acceleration confirmed via `--status` (gpu_compositing enabled). A trace shows INP 668ms with 522ms input delay, Recalculate Style at 88% of bottom-up self time, and single Recalculate Style events of 218.9ms: The forced recalcs come from the editor's own layout path: `applyFontInfo` writes `letter-spacing`, then viewLines reads geometry back (`getClientRects` via `readHorizontalRanges` / `_actualReadPixelOffset`), so every editor pays a forced style recalc per mousemove. That write-then-read pattern is old and normal. What's broken is the cost of each recalc: it now scales with the entire visible DOM instead of the invalidated subtree. ## Cause: :has() rules Minimal measurement, paste into the DevTools console of the workbench window. It appends a childless div directly under `.monaco-workbench`, writes `letter-spacing` on it and reads `offsetHeight` back. That should cost microseconds: ```js (()=>{const w=document.querySelector('.monaco-workbench');let p=document.getElementById('__probe');if(!p){p=document.createElement('div');p.id='__probe';p.textContent='p';p.style.cssText='position:absolute;left:-9999px;top:0';w.appendChild(p)}window.bench0=(n=8)=>{void p.offsetHeight;const t=performance.now();for(let i=0;i{const w=document.querySelector('.monaco-workbench'),reset=()=>{const d=w.style.display;w.style.display='none';void document.body.offsetHeight;w.style.display=d;void document.body.offsetHeight};let n=0;const scan=g=>{let r;try{r=g.cssRules}catch{return}for(let i=r.length-1;i>=0;i--){const x=r[i];if(x.cssRules&&x.cssRules.length)scan(x);if(/:has\(/.test(x.selectorText||'')){g.deleteRule(i);n++}}};for(const s of document.styleSheets)scan(s);reset();return n+' :has rules removed, bench0='+bench0()})() ``` Result on my machine: bench0 goes from 14.263 / 13.387 to 0.037, roughly 375x, and sash dragging is completely smooth again. One detail that cost me a day: deleting the rules alone changes nothing. The invalidation state sticks until you force a full restyle (that's the display toggle inside the script). I suspect this is the same effect that made #324985 "persistent". ## Which rules Per-rule contribution, measured as delete one rule, force full restyle, bench, restore the rule: ```js (()=>{const w=document.querySelector('.monaco-workbench'),reset=()=>{const d=w.style.display;w.style.display='none';void document.body.offsetHeight;w.style.display=d;void document.body.offsetHeight};const es=[];const scan=g=>{let r;try{r=g.cssRules}catch{return}for(let i=0;ib.delta-a.delta);return JSON.stringify({rules:es.length,base,final:bench0(6),top:out.slice(0,10)},null,1)})() ``` Output on my session (72 :has rules total, baseline 13.033ms): | rule | delta (ms) | |---|---| | `.chat-editing-session-list .monaco-scrollable-element:has(.visible.scrollbar.vertical) ...` (chat.css) | **9.958** | | `.command-center .action-item.command-center-center:has(.compact-mode) ...` (titlebar) | 0.808 | | `.rendered-markdown li:has(input[type="checkbox"])` | 0.633 | | `.style-override .monaco-diff-editor:has(> .diffOverview) ...` | 0.483 | | `.chat-confirmation-widget2 ...:has(.chat-agent-feedback-review-list):not(:has(...))` | 0.458 | | ~65 more rules at 0.1-0.4 each | ~3 total | So one rule accounts for 77% of it: ``` .interactive-session .chat-editing-session .chat-editing-session-container.show-file-icons .chat-editing-session-list .monaco-scrollable-element:has(.visible.scrollbar.vertical) .monaco-list-row .monaco-icon-label ``` It only bites once the chat working set list is populated, because the `:has()` anchor has to exist in the DOM. An empty window looks fine, a real working session doesn't. The rest is a long tail. For reference, the workbench CSS bundle went from 73 `:has()` occurrences on 2026-07-02 to 91 today. ## How I got here (bisect trail) I first bisected released insiders with `npx @vscode/vscode-bisect --runtime desktop`: last good `2be9624b8010` (2026-07-02T09:57Z), first bad `688be17ad210` (2026-07-02T15:04Z). To make sure the boundary wasn't a subjective call, I re-ran both builds 4 times each, interleaved, each launch with a fresh empty `--user-data-dir` and `--disable-extensions`, and measured the same write/read pattern against an editor's `.view-lines` instead of trusting how the drag felt: | build | forced recalc ms across 4 fresh launches | DOM element count | |---|---|---| | good `2be9624` | 0.07 / 0.07 / 0.07 / 0.06 | 3166 / 3994 / 2361 / 2367 | | bad `688be17` | 5.79 / 4.71 / 3.35 / 4.56 | 3861 / 2885 / 1986 / 2708 | The bad-side cost tracks the element count almost exactly (about 1.6us per element), which is what pointed at whole-document recalc rather than anything in the editor itself - and indeed none of the 19 commits in that range touch the editor, the layout code, or anything on the trace call stack. The offender inside that range was `body:has(.automation-dialog)` from #323914, which is already fixed (#324985 -> #324986, #325864). Today's insiders regresses anyway because other `:has()` rules do the same thing as soon as their anchors exist. The chat.css rule above predates that range and never showed up in the bisect because the bisect ran on clean profiles with no chat session. Which also means this is a recurring class of regression, not a single bad rule: three instances landed in the last three weeks alone. ## Suggested direction Each of these is fixable the way #324986 fixed the dialog rules: toggle a class from the code that already knows the state. I have a PR ready that fixes the chat.css rule (the class is toggled from `chatInputPart.ts`, which already computes the overflow condition), replaces the remaining root-anchored `:has()` in floatingPanels.css and sessionsPolicyBlocked.css, and adds a stylelint check that rejects new root-anchored `:has()`. The long tail probably deserves an audit by the owning teams; the profiling snippet above should reproduce the ranking on any setup. ## System info ``` CPU - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12950HX (16+8) @ 5.30 GHz GPU - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Mobile [Discrete] GPU - Intel UHD Graphics 770 @ 1.55 GHz [Integrated] MEMORY - 62.41 GiB DISTRO - Arch Linux x86_64 KERNEL - Linux 7.1.4-arch1-1 WM - Hyprland 0.56.0 (Wayland) ```

body:
Title: Ctrl+/ (and possibly other editor keybindings) silently fail under native Wayland ozone platform; works when forced to X11

**Type:** Bug

**Description:**

On Linux with VS Code launched under native Wayland (`--ozone-platform=wayland`, auto-detected via `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`), `Ctrl+/` (Toggle Line Comment) does nothing when pressed as a keyboard shortcut — no error, no visible effect. Running the same command manually via the Command Palette ("Toggle Line Comment") works correctly, so the command and language grammar are fine; only the keybinding dispatch fails.

This happens in **both** English and Russian keyboard layouts, so it is not the known layout/OEM_2 remapping issue (see #287040, which is a different root cause). Explicitly rebinding to `ctrl+oem_2` in `keybindings.json` did not help either.

**Workaround that fixed it:** overriding the launch flags to force XWayland instead of native Wayland (`--ozone-platform=x11` instead of the auto-detected `wayland`) resolved the issue completely — the same `Ctrl+/` keybinding started working immediately after relaunch.

I noticed the running renderer/gpu process had `--enable-features=...,GlobalShortcutsPortal,...` enabled alongside `--ozone-platform=wayland`; flagging in case the global-shortcuts-via-portal path is intercepting/consuming this keystroke before it reaches the focused editor.

**To reproduce:**
1. On a native Wayland GNOME session (tested: Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME 46), launch VS Code normally (auto-detects Wayland).
2. Open any file, select/place cursor on a line.
3. Press `Ctrl+/`. Nothing happens.
4. Run "Toggle Line Comment" from the Command Palette — works fine.
5. Relaunch VS Code with `--ozone-platform=x11` explicitly. Press `Ctrl+/` again — now works.

**Environment:**
- VS Code: 1.129.1 (commit 8a7abeba6e03ea3af87bfbce9a1b7e48fed567b8)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, GNOME Shell 46, Wayland session (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`)
- Not layout-dependent (reproduced in both `us` and `ru` xkb layouts)

title: sessions: open single-file diff directly from single-pane Changes view
body:
Fixes #327012.

## What changed

`SinglePaneChangesViewPane` forced every file click in the Changes view to open the aggregate multi-file diff editor, ignoring the shared single/multi-file decision logic and the Alt invert. This removes that hardcoded override so single-pane falls through to the same logic as the standard layout: it honors the `sessions.changes.openSingleFileDiff` setting (default off, so default behavior is unchanged) with Alt inverting the choice, reusing the existing `_openSingleFileDiffEditor()`/`_openMultiFileDiffEditor()` paths and change-resource abstractions.

Also, when a single-file diff is opened from Changes, it now shows the whole file by default instead of folding unchanged regions — that diff is opened to review one specific file, so nothing should be hidden by default (the aggregate Changes editor keeps its existing Expand/Collapse All actions for the multi-file case).

## Why

Previously, users in the single-pane Agents Window layout always had to open the aggregate Changes editor to see any file's diff — clicking an individual file never opened just that file's diff, unlike the existing editor-window experience.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` — 0 errors
- ESLint — clean
- Hygiene (pre-commit) — passed
- `src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/test/browser` suite — all passing
